name: BCG (Tuberculosis)
recommended_for: UIP context only — given at birth; not relevant to current students, included for schedule completeness
dose_schedule: Single dose, at birth or as early as possible (official schedule allows up to 1 year of age)
price_basis: Free under India's Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) at government facilities; private clinics may add a nominal administration fee (approx. 100-300 INR)
common_side_effects: Small local ulcer/scar at injection site
Mild swelling of local lymph node
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04; price is not from that document (it only lists what's given, not a price) and is general market knowledge, not independently re-verified this session.

name: OPV (Oral Polio Vaccine)
recommended_for: UIP context only — infant doses plus National Immunization Days; not applicable to student-age population
dose_schedule: OPV-0 at birth or within the first 15 days; OPV-1, 2, 3 at 6, 10 and 14 weeks (can be given up to 5 years); OPV booster at 16-24 months
price_basis: Free under UIP; not sold as a standalone retail product for adults/students
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04.

name: IPV (Inactivated Polio Vaccine)
recommended_for: UIP context only — infant doses; not applicable to student-age population
dose_schedule: 2 fractional doses in infancy, at 6 and 14 weeks, per UIP calendar
price_basis: Free under UIP; private IPV where purchased separately is typically low-cost (approx. 300-600 INR/dose)
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04.

name: Pentavalent (DPT-Hep B-Hib)
recommended_for: UIP context only — infant doses; not applicable to student-age population
dose_schedule: 3 primary doses in infancy, at 6, 10 and 14 weeks, per UIP calendar
price_basis: Free under UIP at government centres
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04.

name: Rotavirus Vaccine
recommended_for: UIP context only — infant doses; not applicable to student-age population
dose_schedule: 3 oral doses in infancy, at 6, 10 and 14 weeks (can be given up to 1 year), per UIP calendar
price_basis: Free under UIP at government centres; private brands (Rotavac/Rotasiil) typically 800-1200 INR/dose
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04 — that document notes rotavirus is in phased introduction, not yet universal in every state; private price range is general market knowledge, not independently re-verified this session.

name: PCV (Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine)
recommended_for: UIP context only — infant doses; not applicable to student-age population
dose_schedule: 2 primary doses (6 and 14 weeks) plus 1 booster (9-12 months) per UIP calendar
price_basis: Free under UIP at government centres; private market price commonly cited around 2000-3500 INR/dose
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04 — that document notes PCV is in phased introduction, not yet universal in every state; private price range is general market knowledge, not independently re-verified this session.

name: MR (Measles-Rubella)
recommended_for: UIP context only — doses at 9-12 months and 16-24 months; relevant mainly as a catch-up check for students with incomplete records
dose_schedule: 1st dose at 9-12 months (can be given up to 5 years), 2nd dose at 16-24 months, per UIP calendar
price_basis: Free under UIP at government centres
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04; included for completeness and as a catch-up/verification item.

name: JE (Japanese Encephalitis) — UIP childhood dose
recommended_for: UIP context only — given in JE-endemic districts in childhood; relevant as a catch-up check for students from/moving to endemic areas
dose_schedule: JE-1 at 9-12 months, JE-2 at 16-24 months, in notified endemic districts per UIP calendar
price_basis: Free under UIP in notified endemic districts
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04 — that document notes JE is given in 230 endemic districts, after campaign introduction, not nationwide. See separate adult/traveler JE entry for private pricing.

name: Td (Tetanus-Diphtheria) School-age Booster
recommended_for: UIP context — boosters at 10 and 16 years; relevant as the last government-provided booster before adult Tdap
dose_schedule: Single booster dose at 10 years, another at 16 years (the official schedule also lists separate DPT boosters at 16-24 months and 5-6 years, which are distinct from this Td/TT pair)
price_basis: Free under UIP at government/school-based sessions; private Td/TT shot typically 150-400 INR/dose
source_note: Timing matches the official MoHFW National Immunization Schedule (https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/National%20Immunization%20Schedule.pdf), fetched and cross-checked 2026-11-04; private price range is general market knowledge.

name: Influenza (Flu) Vaccine
recommended_for: Annual vaccination, especially useful for students in hostels/shared living, during exam season, or with respiratory risk factors
dose_schedule: Single dose, repeated annually (quadrivalent strains updated each season)
price_basis: Approx. market range seen across pharmacy/home-vaccination listings (e.g., Influvac Tetra, Fluarix Tetra, Vaxigrip) for the 2025/2026 season; actual price varies by brand, city, and clinic/home-visit fees
source_note: General range from pharmacy/home-vaccination listing pages and health-news coverage of Indian flu vaccination (1mg listings, Business Standard/ThePrint health coverage); not a single competitor's product page.

name: HPV Vaccine — Cervavac (Quadrivalent, India-made)
recommended_for: Girls and young women 9-26 years for cervical cancer prevention; ideal catch-up age for college/university students who missed school-based dosing
dose_schedule: Ages 9-14: 2 doses, at 0 and 6 months. Ages 15-26: 3 doses, at 0, 2 and 6 months.
price_basis: Approx. per-dose price reported in Indian health-news coverage (e.g., ThePrint) comparing cervical cancer vaccines available in India as of early 2024-2025; may have shifted with the national HPV rollout discussion
common_side_effects: Dizziness/fainting (brief, common with HPV vaccines generally — observe 15 min post-shot)
source_note: Comparative pricing from Indian health journalism (ThePrint) cross-checked against general cervical-cancer-vaccine cost articles; not from a single retailer's page.

name: HPV Vaccine — Gardasil 4 / Gardasil 9 (Imported)
recommended_for: Females 9-45 and males 9-15/9-26 (depending on product) for HPV-related cancer and genital wart prevention; relevant for students who prefer the broader-coverage imported brand
dose_schedule: 2 doses (0 and 6-12 months) for younger age bands, or 3 doses (0, 2, 6 months) for older age bands/immunocompromised
price_basis: Wide range reflects Gardasil 4 (~3500-4000 INR/dose) vs. the newer Gardasil 9 (~9000-11000 INR/dose) per Indian health-news coverage; actual price varies significantly by brand, dose count and city
source_note: Comparative pricing from Indian health journalism (ThePrint, Feb 2024) listing Gardasil 4 and Gardasil 9 prices; figures should be re-checked with a current clinic since prices move and the source noted a possible typo in its own Gardasil 9 figure.

name: Hepatitis B Vaccine (Adult)
recommended_for: Adults/students not previously vaccinated or with incomplete childhood series, especially those in healthcare/lab programs or hostels
dose_schedule: 3 doses: 0, 1 and 6 months (standard schedule)
price_basis: General market range for recombinant Hepatitis B vaccine (generic Indian brands at the lower end, branded imports like Engerix-B at the higher end); not taken from a single seller's listing
source_note: Range drawn from general India vaccine-pricing/health-economics discussion (CEHAT publications, pharmacy listings) rather than one retailer; precise current price should be confirmed locally.

name: Hepatitis A Vaccine
recommended_for: Students, especially those moving to new cities/hostels, street-food eaters, or international travelers, without documented immunity
dose_schedule: 2 doses (inactivated, e.g., Havrix/Avaxim), at least 6 months apart; combination Hep A+B (Twinrix) uses 0, 1, 6 months
price_basis: Approx. market range for single-antigen inactivated Hepatitis A vaccines (Havrix, Avaxim) seen across Indian pharmacy price listings; combination Hep A+B products priced separately and higher
source_note: General range from pharmacy drug-price listings (Medindia, 1mg) and health-blog cost overviews (PharmEasy); figure not confirmed from a single competitor's retail page.

name: Typhoid Vaccine (Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine, e.g., Typbar TCV)
recommended_for: Students in hostels/shared mess facilities, new arrivals to a city, or travelers to typhoid-endemic areas
dose_schedule: Single dose (conjugate vaccine, e.g., Typbar TCV), effective for ~3-4+ years; older polysaccharide vaccines need boosting every 2-3 years
price_basis: Wide range reflects basic clinic/government-rate typhoid vaccination at the low end versus bundled home-vaccination-service listings (e.g., a ~2618 INR figure seen on a home-vaccination booking platform, which includes service charges) at the high end
source_note: Range combines a home-vaccination service price point (1mg Typbar TCV listing) with general knowledge of typical clinic pricing for conjugate typhoid vaccines in India; the higher figure likely includes a home-visit service fee rather than vaccine cost alone.

name: Rabies Vaccine (Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis)
recommended_for: Students doing fieldwork/veterinary/animal-handling programs, frequent trekkers, or those in areas with high stray-dog density
dose_schedule: 3-dose pre-exposure series, typically days 0, 7 and 21-28 (intramuscular); intradermal regimens also used by some providers
price_basis: Government-facility doses often cited around 350-800 INR/dose; private clinics typically 800-1200 INR/dose. Figures are general cost-of-rabies-prophylaxis estimates, not pre-exposure-series-specific retail prices
source_note: Price band drawn from a general India rabies-vaccine-cost overview (advancestudy.org) citing government vs private facility ranges; the source noted this may not map exactly onto the pre-exposure (as opposed to post-bite) series, so treat as indicative only.

name: Tdap Vaccine (Adult/Adolescent Booster, e.g., Boostrix)
recommended_for: Students due for their 10-year tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis booster, or before travel/hostel entry where a recent Tdap is required
dose_schedule: Single booster dose, repeated every 10 years (or sooner after injury per clinical advice)
price_basis: Approx. market range for Boostrix and similar Tdap boosters seen across Indian pharmacy/home-vaccination listings
source_note: General range inferred from pharmacy/home-vaccination listing pages for Boostrix (1mg) and general Tdap cost-overview articles; exact current price not independently confirmed this session and should be re-checked.

name: MMR Vaccine (Adult Catch-up)
recommended_for: Students with incomplete/undocumented childhood MMR history, especially before study-abroad or hostel enrollment where proof of immunity is required
dose_schedule: 2 doses, at least 4 weeks apart (for those without documented prior vaccination/immunity)
price_basis: General market range for MMR vaccine in India based on preventive-care/home-vaccination overview pages; precise current price varies by brand and provider
common_side_effects: Joint pain (uncommon, more in adult women)
source_note: Range from general preventive-care vaccine-cost overview content (Bajaj Finserv Markets, Portea-style vaccination pages); not confirmed against a single named brand's current retail price.

name: Varicella (Chickenpox) Vaccine
recommended_for: Students without a history of chickenpox or prior vaccination, especially relevant for hostel/dormitory living
dose_schedule: Adults/older adolescents without prior immunity: 2 doses, 4-8 weeks apart
price_basis: General market range for varicella vaccines (e.g., Varilrix, Varivax) based on health-provider overview pages; exact price was not published on the sources checked and varies by brand/city
source_note: Price is an estimated general range since the specific articles found (Cloudnine, myUpchar) described dosing but explicitly did not publish a rupee figure; treat as indicative and verify locally.

name: Meningococcal Vaccine (e.g., Menactra, ACYW-135)
recommended_for: Students moving into hostels/dormitories, and especially those traveling for study/Hajj or to regions with meningococcal outbreaks
dose_schedule: Single dose for most adolescents/adults (2-dose primary series in some younger pediatric cases); booster every 5 years if ongoing risk continues
price_basis: Approx. range seen in general consumer Q&A and pharmacy references for Menactra in India; higher end reflects a commonly cited community price point of ~4,700-5,700 INR per dose
source_note: Price range includes a parent-forum community answer (FirstCry parenting Q&A) alongside general pharmacy listing presence (Apollo Pharmacy, Truemeds, GNH India); community-sourced figures are not an official price list, so confirm with a clinic.

name: Japanese Encephalitis Vaccine (Adult/Traveler)
recommended_for: Students/travelers heading to or living in JE-endemic rural/agricultural areas of India or other endemic countries, without documented childhood dose
dose_schedule: Live attenuated (SA 14-14-2): single dose. Inactivated (e.g., Ixiaro-type): 2 doses, 28 days apart
price_basis: General range for JE vaccines in India drawn from indigenous-vaccine coverage and travel-health vaccine-cost overviews; price varies significantly by whether a live single-dose or inactivated 2-dose product is used
source_note: Range estimated from general coverage of India's indigenous JE vaccine program and travel-vaccine cost articles; no single current retail price was confirmed this session, so treat as indicative only.

name: COVID-19 Booster Vaccine
recommended_for: Students with risk factors (comorbidities, immunocompromise) or ahead of international travel where a current COVID-19 vaccination certificate may still be requested; mass booster campaigns have wound down since the acute pandemic period
dose_schedule: Single booster dose; frequency/recommendation depends on current government and manufacturer guidance, which has changed repeatedly since 2022
price_basis: Historical range from 2022-era pricing (Covishield/Covaxin cut to 225 INR for government booster drives; Covishield private booster briefly priced around 600 INR) through later heterologous boosters (e.g., Corbevax); availability and official pricing have shifted substantially since, so current price/availability should be verified directly with a provider
source_note: Pricing drawn from 2022-era Indian news coverage (Editorji, Telangana Today) on Covishield/Covaxin/Corbevax booster pricing; this is now dated and COVID-19 booster availability/price in India as of late 2026 should be independently re-verified before use in the live catalog, since mass campaigns have largely ended.
